Reproducibility

How the fictional data were generated

A fixed-seed dispatch-cost model creates job features, missing values and noise. Candidate prediction pipelines are tuned on development folds; a separate held-out set evaluates the frozen procedure.

Fixed seed: 660913. Read the complete generator and analysis code; inspect the saved results.

Known truth: The script controls the cost mechanism and can create a new population for a transport stress test. The final test score is still a finite-sample result, not a universal risk guarantee.

These are model assumptions and generated outcomes, not claims about a real population.

Stop 01 / 24

Write the prediction contract first

Mica is a fictional dispatch network. At request intake, it must forecast the final job cost in credits using only information already known: requested distance, package size, priority, a weather index and origin hub. A forecast made after the job is complete would be a different task even if the outcome column were unchanged.

  • Unit: one independent dispatch request.
  • Scoring moment: intake, before service and billing.
  • Primary target: expected cost for an eligible new request.
  • Primary loss: squared error on the original credit scale.
  • Scope: the generated operating environment and supported input range.

A prediction contract should also state latency, missing-feature handling and a fallback when required inputs are unavailable. We use synthetic costs rather than empirical prices so every assumption and every generated row can be disclosed and reproduced.

Pause and explain

Would a feature recorded only after delivery be eligible because it predicts cost well?

Compare your reasoning
No. It violates the scoring-time information boundary. High predictive association cannot make unavailable future information deployable.

Stop 02 / 24

Let the cost of an error define the target

Squared loss → conditional mean.
Absolute loss → conditional median.
Asymmetric absolute loss cᵤ(Y−a)₊ + cₒ(a−Y)₊ → quantile τ = cᵤ/(cᵤ+cₒ).

An independent log-normal simulation makes the distinction concrete. With underprediction costing four times overprediction, the target is the 80th percentile rather than the mean or median. The table evaluates all three choices on the same 3,000 generated outcomes. Its squared-loss units are credits squared; the other losses are in credits, with cost weights for the asymmetric column.

One distribution, three loss functions
Point rulePredictionMean squared lossMean absolute lossWeighted absolute loss
Mean25.121396.03413.25433.134
Median19.954422.73012.56339.157
80th percentile34.683487.46617.48029.357

For classification, a calibrated probability is not yet an action. A binary decision threshold also depends on false-positive and false-negative costs, and often operational capacity.

Pause and explain

Why can two well-calibrated models disagree about the best point forecast?

Compare your reasoning
They may target different functionals. The mean, median and a cost-weighted quantile need not coincide in a skewed distribution.

Stop 03 / 24

Keep prediction, residual and score distinct

eᵢ = yᵢ−ŷᵢ; MSE = Σeᵢ²/n; RMSE = √MSE; MAE = Σ|eᵢ|/n.

A prediction is one estimated outcome. A residual is one signed miss. A score aggregates misses over a specified sample. RMSE and MAE are in credits; MSE is in credits squared. Mean signed residual reports direction of average error but can be near zero when large positive and negative errors cancel.

Compare models on the same rows, target scale and information set. A baseline fitted on development data establishes whether complexity adds practical value. Our final baseline predicts the development-sample arithmetic mean for every final row. It cannot peek at the final-sample mean.

Large misses receive disproportionate influence under squared loss. Removing or capping high-cost cases changes the scoring population and must be declared before the final audit.

Pause and explain

Can a model with smaller RMSE have larger MAE?

Compare your reasoning
Yes. One may reduce rare large misses while making many ordinary misses slightly worse. The decision’s loss should determine which trade-off matters.

Stop 04 / 24

Explain optimism with repeated training samples

At x: E[(Ynew−f̂(x))²] = σ² + Bias[f̂(x)]² + Var[f̂(x)].

The identity averages over new training samples and independent future noise under a fixed DGP. It is not a decomposition obtained by labelling one fitted residual as “bias” or “variance.” Our separate simulation generates 160 training samples of 45 rows from Y = 8 + 3X + 4X² + Normal(0,2²), X uniform from −1 to 1, then evaluates predictions at a fixed 41-point grid.

Repeated-sample approximation, equal weight on evaluation grid
DegreeMean training MSEEstimated squared biasEstimated varianceNoise varianceEstimated new-outcome risk
15.1681.5810.2694.0005.850
33.6820.0010.4164.0004.418
93.1460.44368.8754.00073.319

The variance term uses the empirical distribution of repeated fitted predictions; the squared-bias term compares their mean with the known curve. The very flexible polynomial can fit training noise and become unstable near the range edges. The risk here is grid-averaged, so do not silently equate it with an integral over another deployment distribution.

Pause and explain

Why do the cross terms disappear in the population derivation?

Compare your reasoning
Centering the estimator around its expectation and assuming independent mean-zero future error makes the relevant expected products zero. A particular finite sample need not have zero realized cross terms.

Stop 05 / 24

Make the new data fully reproducible

log(cost) = 3.2 + 0.035 distance + 0.055 size + 0.12 priority + 0.15 weather
+ 0.012 distance×priority + hub offset + 0.08 sin(distance/3) + 0.28Z.

Seed 660913 generates 604 requests. Distance is Uniform(1,25), size Uniform(1,12), priority Bernoulli(0.25), weather and Z independent standard normal. Hub probabilities are 0.40, 0.35 and 0.25, with log-cost offsets 0, 0.12 and −0.08. Twenty independent standard-normal distractors create a deliberately richer feature set.

Size and weather are independently missing with probability 0.08, and distractor entries with probability 0.05. Missingness is generated after the outcome, independently of the values; this is a teaching assumption, not a claim that real missingness is harmless. The displayed features contain no post-outcome information. The script generates all observations locally and retains the missingness policy explicitly.

Pause and explain

Does a synthetic generator guarantee that every fitted candidate is correctly specified?

Compare your reasoning
No. The candidates omit the sine term, impute missing predictors and impose selected bases. Knowing the generator lets us inspect approximation error instead of pretending it is absent.

Stop 06 / 24

Describe candidates as concrete hypotheses

The candidate feature groups are cumulative, and each has a clear meaning. Core uses distance, size and priority. Context adds weather and two hub indicators. Expanded adds distance squared, size squared, distance×size and distance×priority, plus twenty noise features. All include an intercept; coefficients are fitted to log cost and predictions are smearing-adjusted to credits.

Unpenalized candidate comparison on identical development folds
Feature setDesign columns including interceptTraining RMSE, creditsDevelopment CV RMSE, credits
Core: distance, size, priority426.76827.000
Context: core + weather + hub722.94023.245
Expanded: context + shapes + noise3121.19822.922

A printed coefficient count assumes an identifiable design. A numeric category code is not a substitute for indicator columns. Interactions retain lower-order terms. Candidate columns reflect information available at intake, not what becomes known after completion.

Pause and explain

Why does adding a noise feature sometimes improve a sample score?

Compare your reasoning
Finite samples contain chance correlations. Validation reduces self-fit optimism but itself has sampling noise, especially when many specifications are searched.

Stop 07 / 24

A point forecast does not choose an interval target

A separate fictional crate-quote experiment uses Y = 45 + 10X + 12X² + Normal(0,5²), with 140 observations and X uniform from −1 to 1. At X = 0.5, a correctly specified quadratic predicts 53.146. Its 95% classical mean interval is 52.076 to 54.217, whereas the new-outcome interval is 43.716 to 62.576. Both are computed from the same fitted coefficients.

The mean interval reflects coefficient uncertainty; the prediction interval adds fresh outcome noise. These are an independent normal-theory demonstration, not valid uncertainty bands silently attached to Mica’s tuned LASSO. Penalization, selection, missingness and a transformed outcome require a prediction-uncertainty method designed and calibrated for the actual pipeline.

SE(mean)² = x₀ᵀ V x₀; SE(new outcome)² = x₀ᵀ V x₀ + s² under the stated Gaussian model.

Pause and explain

Can the ordinary OLS standard-error formula be applied unchanged to selected LASSO coefficients?

Compare your reasoning
No. Penalization and data-dependent selection change the estimator’s distribution. Conventional post-selection coefficient intervals are not justified merely because software prints coefficients.

Stop 08 / 24

Back-transform the correct forecast target

ŷmean(x) = exp(m̂(x)) × ŝ; ŝ = mean of exp(training log residuals).

For the constant-noise log-normal generator, the population factor from the noise alone is exp(0.28²/2) = 1.03998. The frozen fitted pipeline’s development-residual smearing factor is 1.04023. It also reflects imperfect fitted structure and imputation, so it need not equal the generator’s factor. A global factor is a modeling choice; conditional residual distributions can differ after missing predictors are imputed.

For the first final row, observed cost is 48.638; exponentiating the fitted log gives 42.437; multiplying by the training smearing factor gives 44.144. Smearing was estimated without any final outcomes. Every CV fold estimates its own factor using that fold’s training residuals.

Exponentiated log quantiles should not automatically receive this mean adjustment. The monotonic transformation of a quantile and correction of an arithmetic mean answer different questions.

Pause and explain

Why not compute one smearing factor using all rows before cross-validation?

Compare your reasoning
It would learn from held-out outcomes and contaminate validation. The full retransformation procedure belongs inside every training fold.

Stop 09 / 24

Connect likelihood to a declared probability model

Independent Gaussian errors: −2 log L = n log(2πσ²) + SSE/σ².
At the maximum: σ̂²ML = SSE/n, so −2 log L̂ = n[log(2π)+1+log(SSE/n)].

Holding the observed data fixed, likelihood compares candidate parameter values under a probability model. For independent Gaussian errors with common variance, maximizing likelihood over coefficients is equivalent to minimizing SSE. The likelihood variance estimate divides by n, unlike the unbiased classical error-variance estimator with denominator n−p.

For independent Bernoulli outcomes the log likelihood is Σ[y log p + (1−y)log(1−p)], so the appropriate likelihood changes with the outcome model. Deviance is a comparison to a specified saturated likelihood; it is not always literally identical to negative twice the log likelihood. State the software convention instead of relying on an unlabeled number.

Pause and explain

Why cannot raw likelihood values from unrelated outcome scales simply be ranked?

Compare your reasoning
They may represent different densities, measures, samples or constants. A transformation requires the appropriate Jacobian to express the likelihood on a common observed-data scale.

Stop 10 / 24

Charge the fit for additional parameters

AIC = −2 log L̂ + 2k.
BIC = −2 log L̂ + k log n.
Same 140 crate-quote observations and Gaussian likelihood convention
Polynomial degreek including error varianceSSEAICBIC
135,258.766910.944919.769
243,075.361837.838849.604
353,075.180839.829854.538
683,033.061843.899867.432

Here k counts regression coefficients, including the intercept, plus one estimated error variance. Lower values are preferred within this declared comparison. AIC targets expected predictive information loss under its approximation; BIC approximates a model-evidence comparison under different assumptions. Neither is a substitute for checking a realistic prediction task.

Do not compare these original-scale Gaussian values directly with a log-outcome fit’s printed values unless the likelihood is expressed on the same outcome scale. For penalized procedures, the appropriate effective degrees of freedom can differ from the raw number of columns.

Pause and explain

Can a lower AIC certify transportability to another market or process?

Compare your reasoning
No. It evaluates a relative fit/complexity trade-off under its assumptions and observed data. Distribution shift remains a separate question.

Stop 11 / 24

Protect the final sample from selection

Before learning any preprocessing parameters, the lab partitions Mica into 453 development rows and 151 final evaluation rows using split seed 660914. It fixes five development folds using seed 660915. The declared final procedure is a standardized expanded-design LASSO on log cost, choosing alpha by minimum pooled development RMSE in credits, followed by a development-only refit and smearing correction.

  • Development folds compare all predeclared alpha values.
  • The selected alpha, feature basis, imputation rule, scaling and correction are frozen.
  • The final sample compares the frozen procedure with its predeclared mean baseline.
  • Final diagnostics describe limitations; they do not trigger further tuning on that sample.

If the final audit causes revisions, those revisions start a new development cycle. Repeatedly inspecting and optimizing a “test” score makes that dataset validation data regardless of its filename.

Pause and explain

Is a random split always the appropriate design?

Compare your reasoning
No. Use time, group, location or another structure when it better imitates the intended new case. The random split here matches the independent generator, not every deployment setting.

Stop 12 / 24

Pool errors before taking a square root

Pooled CV RMSE = √[Σfold SSEfold / Σfold nfold].
Held-out errors for the selected alpha
FoldRowsSquared-error sumFold RMSE
19148,558.08323.100
29139,323.49820.788
39142,868.87921.705
49059,351.35125.680
59045,737.66622.543

The pooled RMSE is 22.817 credits. The unweighted mean of the five fold RMSEs is 22.763. They are not generally identical because the square root is nonlinear, and unequal fold sizes create another weighting difference. Keep every held-out prediction attached to its original row so the overall score and subgroup diagnostics can be reconstructed.

Choosing alpha from these same scores creates selection optimism. The CV minimum is development evidence, not the final unbiased performance claim. Nested CV would be appropriate if the objective were to estimate the performance of the entire tuning procedure without a separate final holdout.

Pause and explain

What exactly is “out of sample” for a CV prediction?

Compare your reasoning
The row’s outcome and learned preprocessing inputs were excluded from that fold’s fitting. It is still part of development and can influence selection through its validation error.

Stop 13 / 24

Treat availability as part of the model

A variable can be present in a historical export but absent at the time a forecast would have been made. Outcome leakage includes final billed amount, a settlement flag, post-service status and any proxy determined after the prediction moment. Splitting rows does not cure this kind of temporal availability error.

Mica’s weather index is stipulated to be known at intake; it is not a realized post-delivery weather summary. Missing size and weather are handled by a training-fitted median policy. Deterministic interactions are then defined on the recorded raw inputs, with missingness propagated, and the resulting design columns are separately median-imputed inside the pipeline.

That order is part of the specification. Imputing raw size first and then squaring it is a different pipeline from median-imputing size squared. Neither should be described vaguely as “we filled missing values.”

Pause and explain

Would an identifier that encodes the final outcome be safe because it is not named “cost”?

Compare your reasoning
No. Audit semantics, lineage and timing, not column names. A proxy can leak the target as effectively as a direct outcome field.

Stop 14 / 24

Put every learned step inside each fold

Training fold → median imputer.fit → scaler.fit → LASSO.fit(log Y) → training smearing.
Validation fold → imputer.transform → scaler.transform → predict → original-scale score.

The pipeline uses SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler and LASSO. Each candidate alpha gets a freshly fitted pipeline inside each fold. The transform parameters learned from training data are retained for that fold’s validation rows. A final refit learns them once again from the complete development set, and those exact values are used for the final sample.

The lab’s development design has 38 missing size entries and 41 missing weather entries. StandardScaler uses a population-style within-training standard deviation, with denominator n. Dummy variables are also scaled in this declared workflow, so their penalization depends on prevalence and must be interpreted accordingly.

Pause and explain

Which steps must be inside the folds if feature selection is added later?

Compare your reasoning
Any selection that learns from the data, whether supervised or unsupervised, belongs inside each training fold. This includes imputation, scaling, transformations with fitted parameters and selected feature lists.

Stop 15 / 24

Ask whether added flexibility earns its place

Unpenalized log-model feature comparison — chart data
GroupDevelopment CV RMSE in credits
Core27.0004
Context23.2451
Expanded22.9222

The context variables contain genuine generator information; the expanded design adds useful shape terms and twenty irrelevant predictors together. The table earlier shows what this particular sample supports. It does not prove that every added feature helps or that all retained coefficients are meaningful. The separate repeated-sample polynomial experiment demonstrates why training fit can keep improving while prediction risk rises sharply.

Compare the entire procedure, not an isolated estimator label. A richer design may need shrinkage, a different missingness policy or more data. The result is conditional on the candidate set, folds, target scale and loss; a low score is not a statement about causal mechanisms.

Pause and explain

Why should the same folds be reused across candidates?

Compare your reasoning
They make scores paired on the same held-out cases, reducing irrelevant variation in the comparison and making row-level error differences inspectable.

Stop 16 / 24

Identify the leak even when its number is small

For the first development fold, the training-only median size is 6.768. The median using all development rows is 6.667, and using development plus final rows it is 6.475. Only the first is appropriate for fitting that fold’s imputer. The complete-development median is appropriate for the final refit, but never for the earlier fold training.

A small difference in these particular medians does not make the leaked procedure correct. Validation is a simulation of future use, when unseen inputs and outcomes cannot help fit preprocessing. The direction and magnitude of leakage bias vary; leakage does not guarantee a more flattering score in every realized sample.

  • Do not compute global medians before splitting.
  • Do not choose categories, knots or selected features from the final sample.
  • Do not use held-out outcomes to estimate a smearing factor.
  • Do not inspect test residuals and then quietly retune alpha.

Pause and explain

Does “unsupervised” preprocessing automatically make global fitting harmless?

Compare your reasoning
No. Learning its parameters from evaluation rows uses information unavailable when fitting for a new case. Keep the training/evaluation boundary intact unless a different transductive task is explicitly intended.

Stop 17 / 24

Shrink coefficients using a declared objective

Minimize (1/2n)Σ(yᵢ−b₀−xᵢᵀb)² + αΣⱼ|bⱼ|.
For one centered predictor with Σxᵢ²/n = 1, z = Σxᵢyᵢ/n:
b̂ = sign(z) max(|z|−α,0).

The intercept is not penalized. For a single standardized coordinate, differentiating the quadratic part and applying the absolute-value subgradient produces soft thresholding. With z = 0.80 and alpha = 0.15, the solution is 0.65. Correlated multivariate predictors require a joint optimization; the one-coordinate expression is an intuition, not a replacement for that fit.

Alpha zero corresponds to unpenalized least squares under this objective, though the script uses LinearRegression rather than asking a LASSO solver to handle zero. Very large alpha can set every slope to zero, leaving an intercept-only log prediction. Objective conventions differ across software, so compare penalties only after checking the scaling.

Pause and explain

Why can LASSO produce exactly zero coefficients?

Compare your reasoning
The absolute-value penalty has a kink at zero. Its subgradient contains an interval, allowing small data gradients to be balanced without a nonzero coefficient.

Stop 18 / 24

Explain what one scaled coefficient means

Independent five-row scaling example
Original inputStandardized input
2-1.414
4-0.707
60.000
80.707
101.414

The mean is 6.000 and StandardScaler-style SD is 2.828. A raw slope of 2.5 corresponds to a standardized-coordinate coefficient of 7.071 because a one-standard-deviation change is 2.828 raw units. The predictions match only if the intercept is transformed consistently too.

zⱼ = (xⱼ−μⱼ)/sⱼ; βraw,ⱼ = βscaled,ⱼ/sⱼ;
b₀,raw = b₀,scaled − Σⱼ βscaled,ⱼ μⱼ/sⱼ.

Without scaling, a penalty can favor one variable merely because its units make its coefficient numerically small. With polynomial and interaction columns, a coefficient describes a change in one design column, not necessarily a feasible isolated change in one raw feature. Use complete design-row contrasts for those inputs.

Pause and explain

Can deployment recompute the mean and SD separately for each new batch of requests?

Compare your reasoning
Not for this frozen pipeline. Use the development-fitted transformation. Re-estimating it changes the meaning of the fitted coefficients and constitutes a changed procedure.

Pause and explain

Is the lowest CV number a perfectly measured advantage over its neighbor?

Compare your reasoning
No. It is a noisy selected minimum. Consider stability, practical score differences and a prespecified simplicity rule when appropriate; do not invent a new rule after seeing the final results.

A selected coefficient list is not a causal explanation

The frozen model retains 27 of 30 penalized design coefficients using a numerical nonzero threshold of 10⁻¹⁰. That is not especially sparse, and several retained columns are known distractors. Pause and explain

If two strongly related predictors exchange nonzero status across resamples, must predictions be unstable?

Compare your reasoning
Not necessarily. Similar combinations can yield stable predictions while individual coefficient selection changes. Assess prediction stability and feature-selection stability separately.

Development mean baseline37.04927.9402.943

The LASSO procedure’s development training RMSE is 21.258, whereas its final RMSE is 23.556. The final log-scale RMSE is 0.319 log units, a different metric with a different weighting of misses. The unadjusted exponentiated-log prediction has final RMSE 24.325 credits; it is shown as a predeclared retransformation diagnostic, not used to change the frozen mean-forecast rule.

This final score is conditional on one split and a finite sample. It estimates performance under the same generator, not a guarantee for tomorrow. If requirements are unmet, report that honestly and return to development without using this sample as a fresh final audit again.

Pause and explain

Does a final score worse than CV prove there was leakage?

Compare your reasoning
No. Sampling variation and selection optimism can create a gap even in a clean pipeline. Investigate the workflow, but do not infer a specific error from a score difference alone.

All 151 final rows appear; no expensive case is cropped away. Above the diagonal means overprediction because predicted cost is on the vertical axis. The high-cost threshold is the development outcome 90th percentile, 116.578 credits, fixed before inspecting final outcomes. Membership in the outcome-defined tail is a retrospective diagnostic, not an intake-time feature.

Conditioning on extreme realized outcomes naturally selects positive noise and can create underprediction even for a calibrated conditional mean. Use this diagnosis to understand risk, not to conclude automatically that adding a tail correction is valid.

Pause and explain

Can the observed-outcome tail label be used to choose a forecast at intake?

Compare your reasoning
No. The realized outcome is not known then. A prospective routing rule must use available predictors and be validated independently.

Stop 23 / 24

A random same-world split is not a future-world test

The lab generates a new 200-row fictional future population after freezing the model. Distances now range from 20 to 40 rather than 1 to 25, and the log-cost mean increases by 0.12. Everything else follows the original generator. This is an explicit stress scenario, not a forecast of a real market.

The development maximum distance is 24.993. In the stress population, 70.5% of requests exceed it. Frozen-model RMSE rises to 63.174 credits, with mean signed residual -21.998. The sign is an observed result of this fitted extrapolation, not something forced by the upward mean shift alone.

Different evaluation populations, same frozen model — chart data
GroupRMSE in credits
Same-world final23.5556
Shifted scenario63.1744

An operational monitoring plan should check feature support, missingness, outcome delay, residual direction and performance by meaningful available subgroups. Define thresholds and responsibility before deployment. A detected shift calls for investigation and a new validation cycle, not automatic reuse of a historical score.

Pause and explain

Is importance weighting enough to repair any transport failure?

Compare your reasoning
No. Weighting may address certain covariate-distribution changes under overlap and stable conditional relationships. It cannot generally fix absent support or a changed outcome mechanism.

Stop 24 / 24

Deliver the strongest claim the audit supports

A concise Mica decision brief says: “We forecast expected job cost at intake using a fully specified log-target LASSO pipeline. Median imputation, scaling, coefficient fitting and smearing occur inside each development fold. The selected alpha 0.00237137 was frozen before final scoring. On 151 same-generator final requests, RMSE was 23.556 credits versus 37.049 for the development-mean baseline. Performance deteriorated materially in the explicitly shifted-distance scenario.”

  • Archive the generator, seeds, exact feature order and split assignments.
  • Keep the complete alpha search, objective convention and optimizer diagnostics.
  • Retain preprocessing parameters, smearing factor and the frozen final scores.
  • Document tail limitations, support boundaries and the next evaluation design.

The downloadable script regenerates all data and re-executes every calculation without external files. The notebook includes the fresh execution output. A useful next exercise changes the prediction loss or missingness process before refitting, then explains which parts of the pipeline and evaluation must change.

Pause and explain

What should happen if the organization changes the task from expected cost to a 90% budget buffer?

Compare your reasoning
Redefine the target and loss, fit an appropriate quantile or predictive distribution procedure, and validate the new decision rule. A mean forecast does not become a calibrated budget buffer by relabelling it.
